corinthians1.10.p1.b1.text: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers …

corinthians1.10.p1.b2.text: … our forefathers were all under the cloud, and that they all passed through the sea.

corinthians1.10.p1.b3.text: … for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.

corinthians1.10.p2.b4.text: Nevertheless, God was not pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness.

corinthians1.10.p2.b5.text: … “The people sat down to eat and to drink, and got up to indulge in revelry.”

corinthians1.10.p2.b6.text: Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.

corinthians1.10.p3.b7.text: So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.

corinthians1.10.p3.b8.text: No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear.

corinthians1.10.p3.b9.text: … But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.

corinthians1.10.p4.b10.text: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

corinthians1.10.p4.b11.text: Is not the cup of blessing that we bless a participation in the blood of Christ? And is not the bread that we break a participation in the body of Christ?

corinthians1.10.p4.b12.text: Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf.

corinthians1.10.p5.b13.text: Consider the people of Israel: Are not those who eat the sacrifices fellow partakers in the altar?

corinthians1.10.p5.b14.text: … the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God.

corinthians1.10.p5.b15.text: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too; you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too.

corinthians1.10.p5.b16.text: Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?

corinthians1.10.p6.b17.text: “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is edifying.

corinthians1.10.p6.b18.text: Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience,

corinthians1.10.p6.b19.text: for, “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof.”

corinthians1.10.p7.b20.text: If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat anything set before you …

corinthians1.10.p7.b22.text: … then do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you and for the sake of conscience—

corinthians1.10.p8.b23.text: So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.

corinthians1.10.p8.b24.text: Do not become a stumbling block, whether to Jews or Greeks or the church of God—

corinthians1.10.p8.b25.text: … For I am not seeking my own good, but the good of many, that they may be saved.
